cross_response_observations:
Across the 24 responses analyzed, several systematic defect patterns emerge in the reasoning strategies employed. 

The most prevalent error is the invalid_one_draw_inference, where many responses incorrectly assume that inspecting a single sequence from an envelope definitively identifies its type. This fails to account for the 7/13 composition of the mixed envelope, where drawing one of the 13 majority-type sequences is indistinguishable from a pure envelope in the initial draw.

A second major pattern is the fatal_wrong_claim, where responses assert that remaining envelope labels are "determined by elimination" or "follow directly" after insufficient inspections. These categorical claims lack valid deductive support because the derangement constraints among three remaining envelopes (with the mixed envelope among them) do not force a unique labeling without additional information.

The not_worst_case pattern appears when strategies assume favorable outcomes, such as the mixed envelope revealing its minority type early, rather than accounting for the adversarial worst-case where all 13 majority-type sequences appear first. Responses also frequently lack missing_lower_bound arguments, asserting minimality without proving that no alternative strategy with fewer inspections could succeed. Several responses exhibit contradictory_final_answer behavior, oscillating among multiple incompatible numeric answers without coherent resolution logic. The wrong_final_number code appears in nearly all incorrect responses, with answers ranging from 1 to 14 instead of the correct 15.
